definition_zh: 展示；陈列；显示；表露；显示屏
definition_en: to put something where it can be seen, or to show a quality, feeling, or image
core_image: 一面折叠的旗子被完全展开
scene: 博物馆的玻璃展柜里灯光正好，讲解员把青铜器摆到最显眼的位置。The museum will display the bronze vessel in a glass case.
sceneCN: 这里 display 是「陈列、展示」（第 1 个义项：把某物放在可见处）；句意：博物馆将把青铜器陈列在玻璃展柜中。

derivatives.zh: display 加表示者的后缀构成，义为「展示者」
display 加 able 构成，义为「可展示的」

senses.title: Put something where it can be seen
senses.definition: to arrange an object so that people can look at it
senses.definitionCN: 摆放物品让人们观看
senses.example: The shop displays its new coats in the window.
senses.exampleCN: 商店把新外套陈列在橱窗里。
senses.why: The first image is a banner unfurled: Old French desploiir meant unfold and spread out, so display is a folded thing opened to view.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初的意象是展开的旗帜。古法语 desploiir 意为「展开、铺开」，所以 display 就是折叠之物被打开给人看。

senses.title: Show a quality or feeling
senses.definition: to let a quality, emotion, or attitude be seen
senses.definitionCN: 让某种品质、情绪或态度被看见
senses.example: He displayed no fear during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨中他没有表现出恐惧。
senses.why: An inner state is treated like a flag: when it becomes visible to others, it is displayed.
senses.whyCN: 内在状态被当作一面旗：当它对别人可见时，就被展示了出来。

senses.title: Show information on a screen
senses.definition: to present data or images on an electronic screen
senses.definitionCN: 在电子屏幕上呈现数据或图像
senses.example: The screen displays the bus number.
senses.exampleCN: 屏幕显示公交车的线路号。
senses.why: The modern screen sense keeps the original idea of spreading something before the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 现代屏幕义保留了最初「铺开在眼前」的想法。

senses.title: An exhibition or a show
senses.definition: an arrangement of objects or effects for people to see
senses.definitionCN: 为观看者布置的物品或效果
senses.example: We watched a fireworks display on the river.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在河边看了一场烟花表演。
senses.why: The noun names the whole arranged spectacle rather than one object.
senses.whyCN: 名词指整个被布置出来的景观，而不是单件物品。

intro.en: Display began with cloth: a folded flag or sail spread open, and the literal unfolding became the model for showing things.
intro.cn: display 从布开始：折叠的旗或帆被展开，字面的展开成为展示万物的模型。

items.en: Latin displicare meant to scatter, to unfold, from dis- apart and plicare to fold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 displicare 意为「散开、展开」，由 dis-（分开）加 plicare（折叠）构成。

items.en: Old French desploiir meant to unfold or spread out a banner or sail.
items.cn: 古法语 desploiir 意为展开旗帜或船帆。

items.en: Around the fourteenth century English took display in the sense of unfurling a flag.
items.cn: 约十四世纪英语借入 display，意为展开旗帜。

items.en: The sense widened from flags to objects, feelings, and spectacles.
items.cn: 词义从旗帜扩大到物品、情绪与景观。

items.en: The word now covers shop windows, screens, and electronic monitors.
items.cn: 如今这个词覆盖橱窗、屏幕与电子显示器。

note.en: These words stand near display in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 display 相邻。

definition_zh: 距离；间距；远处；一段路
definition_en: the amount of space between two places or things
core_image: 两点之间那段量得出来的空
scene: 操场尽头立着旗杆，体育老师用步子一段段量过去。The school is within walking distance of the station.
sceneCN: 这里 distance 是「距离、一段路」（第 1 个义项：两地之间的空间量）；句意：学校离车站步行即到。

senses.title: Space between two places
senses.definition: the amount of space from one place to another
senses.definitionCN: 从一个地方到另一个地方的空间量
senses.example: The distance from home to school is two kilometers.
senses.exampleCN: 从家到学校的距离是两公里。
senses.why: The Latin root stare means to stand: distance is first the space that stands between two points.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 stare 意为「站立」：distance 最先指立在两点之间的那段空。

senses.title: A far-away point or view
senses.definition: a place or view that is far away
senses.definitionCN: 遥远的地方或景物
senses.example: We saw a tower in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 我们看见远处有一座塔。
senses.why: The space between points becomes the far zone where things grow small and blurred.
senses.whyCN: 点与点之间的空，延伸成事物变小、变模糊的远区。

senses.title: Coldness between people
senses.definition: a feeling of not being close or friendly
senses.definitionCN: 不亲近、不友好的感觉
senses.example: There was a polite distance between the two teams.
senses.exampleCN: 两队之间保持着客气而疏远的关系。
senses.why: Physical gap is borrowed for the heart: people who stand far apart are not close.
senses.whyCN: 物理的间隔被借给内心：站得远的人自然不亲近。

intro.en: Distance comes from a Latin verb about standing: it is the space that stands between two things.
intro.cn: distance 来自一个关于「站立」的拉丁动词：它是立在两物之间的那段空。

items.en: Latin distantia comes from distare, to stand apart, from dis- apart and stare to stand.
items.cn: 拉丁语 distantia 来自 distare（分立而站），由 dis-（分开）加 stare（站立）构成。

items.en: Old French distance carried the same sense of space between points.
items.cn: 古法语 distance 保留了点与点之间空间的意思。

items.en: English borrowed distance in the fourteenth century for measured space.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 distance，指可度量的空间。

items.en: The word widened to far-away views and to gaps in time.
items.cn: 词义扩大到远方景物与时间间隔。

items.en: Today distance also names emotional coldness between people.
items.cn: 如今 distance 也指人与人之间的情感疏远。

note.en: These words sit near distance in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 distance 相邻。

definition_zh: 分开；划分；分配；使产生分歧；分界线
definition_en: to separate into parts, or to share out among people
core_image: 一刀把整块蛋糕分成两半
scene: 烘焙课后，老师端出烤好的蛋糕，用长刀从中间划下去。Let us divide the cake into eight equal pieces.
sceneCN: 这里 divide 是「分开、划分」（第 1 个义项：把整体分成若干部分）；句意：我们把蛋糕分成八等份。

derivatives.zh: divide 加名词后缀构成，义为「分开；部门；除法」
division 加形容词后缀构成，义为「引起分裂的」
与 divide 同根的词，义为「被除数；股息」
sub- 加 divide 构成，义为「再分；细分」

senses.title: Separate into parts
senses.definition: to cut or split a whole into pieces
senses.definitionCN: 把整体切开或分成若干块
senses.example: Divide the paper into four squares.
senses.exampleCN: 把纸分成四个方格。
senses.why: Latin dividere means to force apart: a whole is pushed into separate pieces by a line or cut.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dividere 意为「用力分开」：整体被一条线或一刀推成独立的块。

senses.title: Share out among people
senses.definition: to give out portions of something to several people
senses.definitionCN: 把某物分成几份发给众人
senses.example: The children divided the sweets among themselves.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们把糖果分了。
senses.why: Separating is the first step of sharing: each person receives one divided part.
senses.whyCN: 分开是分配的第一步：每人拿到分出的一份。

senses.title: Mathematics: find how many times
senses.definition: to find how many times one number contains another
senses.definitionCN: 求一个数包含另一个数多少次
senses.example: Divide twelve by three and you get four.
senses.exampleCN: 十二除以三等于四。
senses.why: The operation repeatedly takes parts out of a total, so the word for splitting fits it.
senses.whyCN: 这个运算反复从一个总数里取份，所以「分开」一词正好贴合。

senses.title: Cause disagreement
senses.definition: to make people form opposing groups
senses.definitionCN: 使人们形成对立的群体
senses.example: The plan divided the village into two camps.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方案让村民分成两派。
senses.why: A line that cuts a cake can also cut a crowd: people end up on different sides.
senses.whyCN: 切蛋糕的那条线也能切开人群：人们站到了两边。

senses.title: A dividing line or boundary
senses.definition: a line that separates two areas or groups
senses.definitionCN: 分隔两个区域或群体的线
senses.example: The river is the divide between the two farms.
senses.exampleCN: 这条河是两个农场的分界线。
senses.why: The act of separating freezes into the line that does the separating.
senses.whyCN: 分开的动作凝固成那条执行分开的线。

intro.en: Divide comes from a Latin verb about forcing things apart, and that cut still runs through sharing, sums and quarrels.
intro.cn: divide 来自一个拉丁动词，本义是用力分开；这道切口贯穿了分配、算术与争执。

items.en: Latin dividere meant to force apart, to split, related to vidua, a thing cut off.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dividere 意为「用力分开、劈开」，与 vidua（被切下的部分）同族。

items.en: The root appears in the motto divide and rule, dividing peoples to govern them.
items.cn: 词根见于格言 divide and rule（分而治之），即分化民众以便统治。

items.en: Old French diviser carried the sense of splitting and sharing out.
items.cn: 古法语 diviser 承载了劈开与分配的意思。

items.en: English took divide in the fourteenth century for separating wholes into parts.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 divide，指把整体分成部分。

items.en: The word now names the maths operation and social splits as well.
items.cn: 如今这个词也指数学中的除法运算与社会分裂。

note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 divide 相邻。

definition_zh: 做；干；执行；够用；表现；用作助动词
definition_en: to perform an action or task, or to work in a stated way
core_image: 卷起袖子把一件事从头做到尾
scene: 大扫除开始前，妈妈递给他一块抹布，指着窗台上的灰。I will do the windows before lunch.
sceneCN: 这里 do 是「做、干」（第 1 个义项：执行某项任务）；句意：你擦地板，我来擦窗户。

derivatives.zh: do 加表示者的后缀构成，义为「实干者」
do 的动名词，义为「行为；所做的事」
un- 加 do 构成，义为「取消；解开」
over- 加 do 构成，义为「做得过度」

senses.title: Perform an action or task
senses.definition: to carry out a job, duty, or activity
senses.definitionCN: 执行某项工作、任务或活动
senses.example: She does her homework after dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 她晚饭后做作业。
senses.why: Old English don simply meant to make or perform, the plainest word for getting things done.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 don 本义就是「做、执行」，是把事情办成的最朴素的说法。

senses.title: Work or progress in a stated way
senses.definition: to succeed or perform at a level
senses.definitionCN: 达到某种水平或进展
senses.example: He did well in the English exam.
senses.exampleCN: 他英语考试考得不错。
senses.why: Doing a task leads to judging the doing: the verb measures how the work went.
senses.whyCN: 做事自然引出对做法的评价：这个动词开始衡量进展。

senses.title: Be enough or be acceptable
senses.definition: to be sufficient or suitable
senses.definitionCN: 足够或合适
senses.example: Any pen will do for the note.
senses.exampleCN: 写个便条，什么笔都行。
senses.why: A task finished adequately is done, so do slides into meaning enough.
senses.whyCN: 把活干到合格就算 done，于是 do 滑向「足够、可以」。

senses.title: Helping verb in questions and negatives
senses.definition: used to form questions and negatives
senses.definitionCN: 用于构成疑问句和否定句
senses.example: Do you like rice? I do not know.
senses.exampleCN: 你喜欢米饭吗？我不知道。
senses.why: The plain action verb thinned into a grammatical tool that only carries tense and person.
senses.whyCN: 这个朴素的实义动词虚化成了只承载时态和人称的语法工具。

intro.en: Do is one of the oldest English verbs, a plain word for making things happen.
intro.cn: do 是英语最古老的动词之一，一个让事情发生的朴素词。

items.en: Old English don meant to make, to perform, to put.
items.cn: 古英语 don 意为做、执行、放置。

items.en: The root goes back to Germanic forms related to putting and setting.
items.cn: 词根可追溯到日耳曼语族中与「放置」相关的形式。

items.en: The verb spread as a helper in questions and negatives.
items.cn: 在中古英语期，它扩展为疑问句和否定句中的助动词。

items.en: Done became the everyday mark of a finished task.
items.cn: done 成为事情完成的日常标记。

items.en: Modern English uses do everywhere: doing sums, doing well, do come in.
items.cn: 现代英语中 do 无处不在：doing sums（算题）、doing well（干得好）、do come in（请进）。

definition_zh: 医生；大夫；博士；修理工（口语）
definition_en: a person trained to treat sick people, or someone holding the highest university degree
core_image: 白大褂口袋里插着听诊器
scene: 候诊室里孩子咳个不停，护士示意他们进诊室。The doctor listened to his chest with a stethoscope.
sceneCN: 这里 doctor 是「医生」（第 1 个义项：看病治病的人）；句意：医生用听诊器听他的胸腔。

derivatives.zh: doctor 加名词后缀构成，义为「博士学位」

senses.title: A person who treats the sick
senses.definition: a trained person who treats illness
senses.definitionCN: 受过训练、治疗疾病的人
senses.example: The doctor gave her some medicine for the cough.
senses.exampleCN: 医生给她开了治咳嗽的药。
senses.why: Latin docere means to teach: one who has been taught deeply becomes the one whose word we follow.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 docere 意为「教导」：被深度教导出来的人，成了人们听从其话的人。

senses.title: Holder of the highest degree
senses.definition: a person with the top university degree
senses.definitionCN: 拥有大学最高学位的人
senses.example: She is a doctor of physics.
senses.exampleCN: 她是物理学博士。
senses.why: The teaching root stays: a doctor is one qualified to teach the deepest subject matter.
senses.whyCN: 「教导」的词根仍在：博士是有资格讲授最深学问的人。

senses.title: To change something dishonestly
senses.definition: to change something secretly to deceive
senses.definitionCN: 暗中改动以欺骗他人
senses.example: Someone doctored the photo.
senses.exampleCN: 有人篡改了那张照片。
senses.why: The expert's careful touch turned into an unskillful misuse: arranging facts the way a doctor arranges a body.
senses.whyCN: 行家的妙手变成了歪用：像医生摆弄身体那样摆弄事实。

intro.en: Doctor began as a Latin word for teacher, and the healing sense grew out of learning.
intro.cn: doctor 起初是拉丁语的「老师」，治病之义从学问中长出。

items.en: Latin doctor meant teacher, from docere, to teach.
items.cn: 拉丁语 doctor 意为教师，来自 docere（教导）。

items.en: Medieval Latin used doctor for learned masters of law, theology and medicine.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语用 doctor 称呼法律、神学与医学的大学者。

items.en: Old French doctour carried the word into everyday speech.
items.cn: 古法语 doctour 把这个词带入日常语言。

items.en: English used doctor for learned men and later chiefly for healers.
items.cn: 英语先用 doctor 称学者，后来主要指治病者。

items.en: The degree sense and the informal fake sense both survive today.
items.cn: 如今学位义与口语中「篡改」义都保留了下来。

abstract.en: Notice one date quietly changed in a document.

definition_zh: 文件；公文；证件；文献；记录
definition_en: a piece of paper or digital file that gives information or proves something
core_image: 盖着红章的证明文件摆在桌上
scene: 入境大厅前排着长队，他把护照从文件袋里抽出来。The officer checked every document at the border.
sceneCN: 这里 document 是「证件、文件」（第 1 个义项：证明或提供信息的材料）；句意：边检人员查验每一份证件。

derivatives.zh: document 加后缀构成，义为「纪录片」
document 加名词后缀构成，义为「文档；证明材料」

senses.title: A paper or file that proves or informs
senses.definition: a written or printed paper, or a digital file, giving proof or information
senses.definitionCN: 提供证明或信息的书面、打印或电子材料
senses.example: Please bring an identity document to the exam.
senses.exampleCN: 考试请携带身份证件。
senses.why: Latin docere means to teach: a document is a thing that teaches the reader what is true.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 docere 意为「教导」：document 就是向读者「讲明」真相之物。

senses.title: A historical written record
senses.definition: an old written record kept for study
senses.definitionCN: 供研究保存的古老书面记录
senses.example: Historians studied the documents of the Ming court.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家研究明代的宫廷文献。
senses.why: Records preserved in writing keep teaching later generations, so the teaching root survives.
senses.whyCN: 以文字保存的记录持续教导后人，「教导」词根得以延续。

senses.title: To prove or record with evidence
senses.definition: to support a claim with written evidence
senses.definitionCN: 用书面证据支持某个说法
senses.example: The reporter documented every step of the story.
senses.exampleCN: 记者为报道的每一步留档佐证。
senses.why: The noun turns into a verb: what the paper teaches becomes what the writer records.
senses.whyCN: 名词转为动词：纸上讲明的内容，变成写作者记录的内容。

intro.en: Document began as a Latin word for a lesson: something that teaches.
intro.cn: document 起初是拉丁语里的「课程」：能教导人的东西。

items.en: Latin documentum meant a lesson or warning, from docere, to teach.
items.cn: 拉丁语 documentum 意为课程或警示，来自 docere（教导）。

items.en: The root doc- also gave doctor, doctrine and docile.
items.cn: 词根 doc- 还派生出 doctor、doctrine 与 docile。

items.en: Old French document meant instruction and later a written paper.
items.cn: 古法语 document 先指教导，后指书面文件。

items.en: English borrowed it in the fifteenth century for teaching and proof.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入该词，指教导与凭证。

items.en: The word now covers passports, archives and computer files.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖证件、档案与计算机文件。

sceneCN: 这里 documentary 是「纪录片」（第 1 个义项：讲真实事实的影片）；句意：全班观看了一部关于野生大熊猫的纪录片。

senses.title: A film of real facts
senses.definition: a film or programme giving facts about real life
senses.definitionCN: 讲述真实生活事实的电影或节目
senses.example: The documentary follows whales across the ocean.
senses.exampleCN: 这部纪录片追踪鲸鱼横渡大洋。
senses.why: The word is built on document: the film is treated as a moving paper of evidence.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在 document 之上：影片被当作一页会动的证据纸。

senses.title: Based on written records

senses.definitionCN: 基于文件或使用文献的
senses.example: The film used documentary evidence from the war.
senses.exampleCN: 影片引用了战争时期的书面证据。
senses.why: The adjective keeps the paper sense: proof still comes from documents.

senses.title: The common pet animal
senses.definition: a four-legged animal kept as a pet or for work
senses.definitionCN: 被人饲养作宠物或用于工作的四足动物
senses.example: Our dog barks at the postman every morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我们家的狗每天早晨都冲邮递员叫。
senses.why: The old Germanic word hund gave way to dog, whose origin itself is uncertain, but the animal image never changed.
senses.whyCN: 古老的日耳曼词 hund 后来让位给 dog，其来源本身不确定，但狗的形象从未改变。

senses.title: A male dog or a contemptible person
senses.definition: a male dog, or a rude word for a person
senses.definitionCN: 公狗，或对人的粗俗称呼
senses.example: In the old tale the dog stole a bone.
senses.exampleCN: 老故事里那家伙偷了一根骨头。
senses.why: Calling a person an animal insults them, so dog slid into name-calling.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫成动物是羞辱，于是 dog 滑向骂人的话。

senses.title: To follow closely and refuse to leave

senses.example: Doubts dogged him for years.
senses.exampleCN: 疑虑多年来一直纠缠着他。
senses.why: The loyal pet that follows its owner became the image of trouble that will not leave.
senses.whyCN: 寸步不离主人的忠犬，变成了甩不掉的麻烦的画面。

definition_zh: 美元；元（美国、加拿大、澳大利亚等货币单位）
definition_en: the unit of money used in the United States and several other countries
core_image: 绿色纸币上印着一位老总统的头像
scene: 小卖部柜台上摆着价签，他数出几张纸币。The toy costs twenty dollars.
sceneCN: 这里 dollar 是「美元」（第 1 个义项：美国等国的货币单位）；句意：这个玩具要二十美元。

derivatives.zh: dollar 加化用后缀构成，义为「美元化」
dollar 构成的复合形容词，义为「以美元计价的」

senses.title: The American money unit
senses.definition: the basic money unit of the United States
senses.definitionCN: 美国的基本货币单位
senses.example: A sandwich here costs five dollars.
senses.exampleCN: 这里一个三明治五美元。
senses.why: The money name traveled from a mine town in Bohemia to the paper bills in your pocket.
senses.whyCN: 这个货币名从波希米亚的一座银矿小镇一路走到你口袋里的纸币。

senses.title: Money or wealth in general

senses.example: He made his dollars by fixing bikes.

senses.why: One coin stands for all coins: the unit becomes money itself.

intro.en: Dollar began in a Bohemian silver valley, not in America.
intro.cn: dollar 起源于波希米亚的一条银矿山谷，而不是美洲。

items.en: Thaler came from Joachimsthaler, a coin struck at Sankt Joachimsthal, the valley of Saint Joachim.
items.cn: Thaler 来自 Joachimsthaler，即圣约阿希姆谷（Sankt Joachimsthal）铸造的银币。

items.en: The word tal has been linked by some scholars to Germanic and Scandinavian roots for counting or valley.

items.en: In the eighteenth century the young United States chose dollar as its money unit.
items.cn: 十八世纪，年轻的美国选择 dollar 作为货币单位。

definition_zh: 门；门户；门口；通道
definition_en: a flat movable panel that opens an entrance to a room or building
core_image: 一扇虚掩的木门透出一线光
scene: 傍晚他到家门口，钥匙还没插进锁孔，门就开了。Please close the door behind you.
sceneCN: 这里 door 是「门」（第 1 个义项：出入房间的可开合板）；句意：请随手关门。

collocations.zh: 为……打开大门；使成为可能

derivatives.zh: door 加 way 构成，义为「门口；门道」
out 加 door 构成，义为「户外的」
door 加 man 构成，义为「门卫；门童」

senses.title: The movable panel of an entrance
senses.definition: a panel that opens and closes an entrance
senses.definitionCN: 开合出入口的活动板
senses.example: The wooden door creaks when it opens.
senses.exampleCN: 木门打开时会吱呀作响。
senses.why: Old English duru named the leaf you push: the simplest barrier that lets people in or keeps them out.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 duru 指你推的那扇门叶：最简单的屏障，放人进来或把人挡在外面。

senses.title: The entrance or doorway itself
senses.definition: the opening or passage into a building
senses.definitionCN: 进入建筑物的开口或通道
senses.example: A crowd stood at the door of the hall.
senses.exampleCN: 一群人站在礼堂门口。
senses.why: The panel stands for the whole opening it guards.
senses.whyCN: 门板代表它看守的整个开口。

senses.title: A way to reach or enter something
senses.definition: a means of getting into or reaching something
senses.definitionCN: 进入或到达某物的手段
senses.example: Hard work is the door to success.
senses.exampleCN: 努力是通往成功之门。
senses.why: A gate for feet becomes a gate for chances: the passage image widens.
senses.whyCN: 让脚通过的门，变成让机会通过的门：通道的意象被拓宽。

intro.en: Door is one of the oldest English words, as old as the doorway itself.
intro.cn: door 是英语最古老的词之一，与门道一样古老。

items.en: Old English duru and dor meant door, gate, passage.
items.cn: 古英语 duru 与 dor 意为门、大门、通道。

items.en: The root goes back to Germanic dhur-, related to words for door in many old languages.
items.cn: 词根可追溯到日耳曼语 dhur-，与多种古语中的「门」一词同源。

items.en: Related Norse and Germanic forms kept the same core meaning.
items.cn: 同族的诺斯语与日耳曼语形式保留了相同的核心义。

items.en: The spelling settled as door, replacing older dor.
items.cn: 拼写定型为 door，取代了旧的 dor。

items.en: The word now names panels, entrances and open chances.
items.cn: 如今这个词指门板、出入口与开放的机会。

note.en: These words sit near door in form or meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 door 相邻。

definition_zh: 两倍的；加倍的；双人的；翻倍；对折
definition_en: twice as much or as many, or to make something twice as large
core_image: 两张一模一样的纸叠在一起
scene: 运动会上，接力赛最后一棒冲线，全场分数翻了番。Sales doubled after the shop opened a second floor.
sceneCN: 这里 double 是「翻倍」（第 2 个义项：变成两倍）；句意：商店开了二楼后，销售额翻了一番。

derivatives.zh: double 加指小后缀构成，义为「紧身衣；（语言学）同源对偶词」
double 加副词后缀构成，义为「加倍地」
double 的动名词，义为「加倍；对折」

senses.title: Twice as much or as many
senses.definition: being twice the size, number, or amount
senses.definitionCN: 大小、数量或程度是两倍
senses.example: She paid double the usual price.
senses.exampleCN: 她付了平时两倍的价钱。
senses.why: Latin duplus means twofold: one folded thing laid on another makes the pair image.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 duplus 意为「两层的」：一物对折压在另一物上，便有了成对的画面。

senses.title: To become twice as large
senses.definition: to become twice as much or as many
senses.definitionCN: 变成原来的两倍
senses.example: The village doubled in size in ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 十年间村子规模翻了一番。
senses.why: If a thing doubles, the pair image grows: one becomes two without cutting.
senses.whyCN: 东西翻倍时，成对的画面长大：一变成二，无需切分。

senses.title: Made for two people
senses.definition: made for or holding two persons
senses.definitionCN: 供两人使用或容纳两人
senses.example: They booked a double room by the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在海边订了一间双人房。
senses.why: The pair of sheets becomes a pair of sleepers: two of the same share one thing.
senses.whyCN: 成对的东西变成成对的人：两个相同者共享一件事物。

senses.title: To bend or fold over
senses.definition: to bend something so one part lies on another
senses.definitionCN: 把某物折弯使一部分压在另一部分上
senses.example: He doubled the paper and put it in his pocket.
senses.exampleCN: 他把纸对折后放进口袋。
senses.why: The original folding action survives in paper and cloth.
senses.whyCN: 最初的对折动作在纸与布上留存了下来。

intro.en: Double carries the old idea of two folded together, one lying on one.
intro.cn: double 承载着「两层叠在一起、一压着一」的古老意象。

items.en: Latin duplus meant twofold, from duo two and plus fold.
items.cn: 拉丁语 duplus 意为两层的，由 duo（二）加 plus（折叠）构成。

items.en: Old French doble carried the word into Romance speech.
items.cn: 古法语 doble 把这个词带入罗曼语系。

items.en: English borrowed double in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语借入 double。

items.en: The sense spread from amounts to rooms, sports and folding.
items.cn: 词义从数量扩展到房间、运动与折叠。

items.en: Modern English keeps the adjective, verb and noun together.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了它的形容词、动词与名词用法。

definition_zh: 怀疑；疑问；不确定；怀疑（某事不真）
definition_en: a feeling of not being sure, or to think something may not be true
core_image: 站在岔路口不敢迈步的人
scene: 交卷前最后一秒，他盯着第七题的答案迟迟不肯改。She had no doubt that her answer was right.
sceneCN: 这里 doubt 是「怀疑、不确定」（第 1 个义项：对真假拿不准的感觉）；句意：她毫不怀疑自己的答案是对的。

derivatives.zh: doubt 加形容词后缀构成，义为「可疑的；不确定的」
doubt 加后缀构成，义为「无疑地」
doubt 加否定前缀再加副词后缀构成，义为「毫无疑问地」

senses.title: Not sure if something is true
senses.definition: a feeling of uncertainty about truth or success
senses.definitionCN: 对真假或成败拿不准的感觉
senses.example: There is some doubt about the date of the event.
senses.exampleCN: 这件事的日期还有些不确定。
senses.why: Latin dubitare means to waver: the mind hesitates between two paths like a walker at a fork.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为「摇摆」：心在两条路之间犹豫，像站在岔路口的人。

senses.title: Think something may be false
senses.definition: to believe something may not be true
senses.definitionCN: 认为某事可能不真实
senses.example: I doubt that he will come so early.
senses.exampleCN: 我不太相信他会来这么早。
senses.why: Wavering tilts toward disbelief: one of the two paths is chosen in the heart.
senses.whyCN: 摇摆偏向不信：心里的两条路已暗暗选了一条。

senses.title: A reason to question or disbelieve
senses.definition: a reason for questioning a claim
senses.definitionCN: 质疑某个说法的理由
senses.example: The report cast doubt on the old numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 报告让人对旧数据产生了疑问。
senses.why: The inner wavering becomes an outer question that others must answer.
senses.whyCN: 内心的摇摆变成必须由他人回答的外部质疑。

intro.en: Doubt grows from a Latin verb about wavering between two paths.

items.en: Latin dubitare meant to waver, to hesitate, related to duo, two.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dubitare 意为摇摆、犹豫，与 duo（二）相关。

items.en: Dubius meant doubting, unclear, a mind pulled two ways.
items.cn: dubius 意为可疑的、不清楚的，即被两个方向拉扯的心。

items.en: Old French douter meant to fear and to doubt.
items.cn: 古法语 douter 兼有恐惧与怀疑之义。

items.en: English took doubt around the thirteenth century, keeping the b in spelling.
items.cn: 约十三世纪英语借入 doubt，拼写保留了 b。

items.en: The b stays in spelling though it is silent in speech.
items.cn: 如今 b 在书写中保留，在口语中不发音。

senses.title: Toward a lower place
senses.definition: moving to or staying at a lower level
senses.definitionCN: 移向或处于更低的位置
senses.example: He climbed down from the wall.
senses.exampleCN: 他从墙上爬了下来。
senses.why: Old English adune meant from the hill: going off the high ground toward the valley.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 adune 意为「离开山丘」：从高地走向谷底。

senses.title: In a lower position or level
senses.definition: situated at a lower point or amount
senses.definitionCN: 位于更低的点或更少的量
senses.example: The sun is down and the street lights come on.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳落山，路灯亮起。
senses.why: Once you leave the hill you stay off it: movement becomes state.
senses.whyCN: 离开山丘后便处于山脚：动作变成状态。

senses.title: Sad or low in spirits
senses.definition: feeling sad or without energy

senses.example: She felt down after failing the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试失利后她情绪低落。
senses.why: Down on the ground feels heavy and low, so feelings borrow the direction.

senses.title: A play for the stage
senses.definition: a serious play written to be performed
senses.definitionCN: 为演出而写的严肃剧目
senses.example: The drama tells of a fisherman and the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 这部戏讲的是一个渔夫与大海的故事。
senses.why: Greek dran means to do: a drama is a story done, acted out before your eyes.

senses.title: An exciting real-life event

senses.example: The rescue was full of drama.

senses.why: Real life begins to look like a staged play: tension, turns and a climax.

senses.title: Exaggerated excitement

senses.definitionCN: 对小事反应过度
senses.example: Do not make a drama out of a lost pencil.
senses.exampleCN: 别为丢一支铅笔大惊小怪。
senses.why: Stage emotion spills onto small events: everything is performed too loudly.
senses.whyCN: 舞台情绪泼洒到小事上：一切都演得太夸张。

definition_zh: 梦；梦想；做梦；向往
definition_en: a series of pictures in the mind during sleep, or a strong hope for the future
core_image: 闭眼后脑海里放起的无声电影
scene: 午休的教室里，他把脸埋进臂弯，梦里已是世界杯的决赛场。He had a strange dream about flying last night.
sceneCN: 这里 dream 是「梦」（第 1 个义项：睡眠中脑中出现的景象）；句意：昨晚他做了一个关于飞翔的怪梦。

derivatives.zh: dream 加表示者后缀构成，义为「做梦的人；空想家」
dream 加形容词后缀构成，义为「梦幻般的；恍惚的」
day 加 dream 构成，义为「白日梦」
与 dream 相关的反义意象，义为「噩梦」

senses.title: Pictures in the mind during sleep
senses.definition: images and events in the mind while sleeping
senses.definitionCN: 睡眠时脑中出现的图像与情景
senses.example: I had a dream that I was swimming.
senses.exampleCN: 我梦见自己在游泳。
senses.why: Old English dream first meant joyful noise; the sleeping pictures took over the word later.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 dream 最初指欢快的声响；后来睡眠中的画面接管了这个词。

senses.title: A strong hope for the future
senses.definition: something you strongly wish to achieve
senses.definitionCN: 非常渴望实现的事
senses.example: Her dream is to become a doctor.
senses.exampleCN: 她的梦想是成为一名医生。
senses.why: Sleeping pictures are wishes that feel real, so waking hopes borrowed the same word.
senses.whyCN: 睡梦中的画面逼真得像愿望成真，于是醒着的希望借用了同一个词。

senses.title: To imagine or wish idly
senses.definition: to let the mind wander to pleasant fancies
senses.definitionCN: 任思绪漂向美好的幻想
senses.example: He sat dreaming of the summer sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他坐着幻想夏日的海。
senses.why: The mind plays its own film when the eyes do nothing.
senses.whyCN: 眼睛闲着时，心里自会放映它的电影。

intro.en: Dream began as a sound of joy, and only later became the film in your sleep.
intro.cn: dream 起初是欢乐之声，后来才变成你睡梦中的电影。

items.en: Old English dream meant joy, mirth, music making.
items.cn: 古英语 dream 意为欢乐、喜庆、奏乐。

items.en: Norse draumr meant a sleeping dream, closely related in form.
items.cn: 诺斯语 draumr 意为睡眠之梦，形式上 closely related。

items.en: The sleeping sense, helped by Norse, replaced the joy sense.
items.cn: 在诺斯语的助推下，睡眠义取代了欢乐义。

items.en: Dream came to name both night visions and day hopes.
items.cn: dream 开始兼指夜间幻象与白日的希望。

items.en: Modern English keeps noun and verb side by side.
items.cn: 现代英语保留其名词与动词用法。

definition_zh: 连衣裙；衣服；穿衣；打扮

sceneCN: 这里 dress 是「穿衣」（第 2 个义项：给自己或他人穿衣服）；句意：孩子们每天早上七点前穿好衣服。

senses.title: A one-piece garment
senses.definition: a single garment covering body and legs
senses.definitionCN: 连身上下成一体的裙装
senses.example: She wore a red dress to the party.
senses.exampleCN: 她穿红裙子去参加聚会。
senses.why: Old French dresser meant to arrange and set straight: cloth arranged on the body became the dress.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 dresser 意为「整理、摆放端正」：布料被端正地摆在身上，便成了连衣裙。

senses.title: Put clothes on
senses.definition: to put clothes on yourself or someone
senses.definitionCN: 给自己或他人穿上衣服
senses.example: Dress warmly; it is cold outside.
senses.exampleCN: 多穿点，外面很冷。
senses.why: Arranging cloth on the body is dressing: the setting action turns into putting on.
senses.whyCN: 把布料安排到身上就是穿衣：摆放的动作变成穿的动作。

senses.title: Make neat or arrange
senses.definition: to arrange or set something in order
senses.definitionCN: 把某物摆放整齐
senses.example: The gardener dressed the flower beds.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁整理了花坛。
senses.why: The original French sense of setting straight survives here.
senses.whyCN: 法语原义「摆放端正」在这里留存。

senses.title: Treat a wound

senses.definitionCN: 清洁并覆盖伤口
senses.example: The nurse dressed the cut on his arm.
senses.exampleCN: 护士包扎了他手臂上的伤口。
senses.why: Arranging clean cloth on the body once more, now for healing.
senses.whyCN: 又一次把干净的布「摆」到身上，这次是为了愈合。

core_image: 水杯倾斜，水流滑进喉咙

senses.title: Drink alcohol

senses.title: A liquid for drinking

senses.definitionCN: 解渴的液体
senses.example: Cold drinks are sold at the gate.

senses.why: The act turns into its object: what you drink is a drink.
senses.whyCN: 动作转指对象：你喝的东西就叫 a drink。

senses.title: A single serving of alcohol

senses.example: They raised a drink to the new year.
